name: Verifiable credentials and decentralized identity (W3C VC 2.0, DIDs, UNTP, EU wallet, EBSI)
scope_note: Covers DPP implementations in which the passport and its supporting claims are published as W3C Verifiable Credentials (VCDM 2.0) secured by JOSE/COSE envelopes or Data Integrity proofs, with issuers identified by DIDs (did:web, did:webvh) and status published as Bitstring Status Lists. The UN Transparency Protocol (UNTP 0.7.0 pilots release and the Work in Progress / v0.8.0 candidate) is the main DPP-specific profile. Its reference tooling (tests-untp, VCkit, storage service, identity resolver) and the W3C VC test suites are recorded as implementations. OpenID4VCI/OpenID4VP, VCALM (formerly VC API), SD-JWT, the EU Digital Identity Wallet and EBSI/TRACE4EU are recorded as context only. Left out: the normative text of any EN/ISO/IEC/DIN document (bibliographic metadata only), the content of Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (EUR-Lex returned empty content to the fetch tool), the EUDI Architecture and Reference Framework content (repository metadata only), EBSI API specifications, DIDComm, AnonCreds/Hyperledger Indy, BBS cryptosuites, blockchain-anchored DID methods (covered by the DLT family), and any live resolver, DID document, status list, wallet or EBSI endpoint (none was called). UNTP text is described in own words only; its licence is unresolved (catalogue record untp-dcc-0-7-0; the page was re-fetched on 2026-10-19 and its footer still says CC BY 4.0, while the repositories are GPL-3.0). ESPR provisions: the consolidated text (which omits recitals) was word-searched in full in the continuation pass; recitals were not searched because EUR-Lex returned empty content.
summary: In this method each DPP statement is a signed, self-contained W3C Verifiable Credential: the manufacturer issues a Digital Product Passport credential, conformity assessment bodies issue conformity credentials, facility operators issue facility records, and traceability events link input and output batches. Credentials follow VCDM 2.0 (base context https://www.w3.org/ns/credentials/v2 first in @context) and are secured either by an enveloping proof (JWT with typ vc+jwt, SD-JWT, or COSE_Sign1) or by an embedded Data Integrity proof (cryptosuites such as eddsa-jcs-2022, eddsa-rdfc-2022, ecdsa-rdfc-2019, ecdsa-jcs-2019, ecdsa-sd-2023). UNTP 0.7.0 fixes the profile to VCDM 2.0 with the JOSE enveloping proof, did:web or did:webvh issuer identifiers, Bitstring Status List for revocation, and an optional HTML render template. Issuer keys are found by dereferencing the kid (a DID URL) to a verification method in a DID or controlled identifier document; for did:web the DID maps to an HTTPS URL ending in did.json, and for did:webvh to a hash-chained did.jsonl log. Discovery starts at the product's data carrier: the carrier encodes a resolver URL; an Identity Resolver (a GS1-conformant resolver pattern extended by UNTP) redirects to a default link or returns an RFC 9264 linkset whose typed links (dpp, dcc, dfr, dte, idr) point at credentials. A verifier then fetches the credential, checks the signature with the resolved key, validates the envelope and the UNTP JSON Schema and contexts, fetches and verifies the status list credential, and reads the bit at statusListIndex. Issuer trust is not given by the signature alone: UNTP adds a Digital Identity Anchor credential issued by an authoritative register that binds the issuer DID to a registered identifier, and lists of trusted registrars. Restricted data uses encrypted link targets (symmetric keys, minimum 128 bits) whose keys travel with the product or are released after DID-based authentication or OpenID4VP. In the EU, Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 Art. 11 requires data authentication, reliability and integrity and empowers an implementing act on issuing and verifying digital credentials of actors with access rights (not adopted at retrieval; a Commission slide deck targets Q2 2027), and Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 Art. 4 already accepts electronic attestations of attributes and qualified seals to verify DPP registry users. For a black-box conformance engine the method is attractive because almost every property is observable from signed artifacts, but today's integrity.jws check cannot verify any credential of this family: it requires typ dpp+jws, an x5c chain and only the headers alg, kid, typ and x5c.

maturity.adoption_evidence: UNTP describes itself as suitable for pre-production pilots; its sample credentials form a copper-to-battery chain (mine, refinery, battery maker). The UN/CEFACT tooling (VCkit 1.2.1, storage service v4.0.0, Pyx identity resolver v4.0.0 per tests-untp version.json) is active in 2026. The W3C implementation registry lists 23 implementer files (for example TrustVC registers did:web issuer and verifier endpoints for ecdsa-sd-2023). EBSI's TRACE4EU project piloted EBSI verifiable credentials for battery passport supply-chain data (LEI, product carbon footprint, responsible mining certificate, due diligence report); HaDEA reports a demonstrated issuance and verification of a battery DPP, without public deliverables or code located. Peer-reviewed evidence is mostly prototypes and simulations (DID/VC DPP performance study, Hyperledger Fabric with cheqd DIDs, EBSI seafood traceability, UNTP-aligned VCs on a zkEVM testnet); no production-scale deployment study was located.
maturity.regulatory_alignment: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 Art. 11 first subparagraph point (g) requires that DPP data authentication, reliability and integrity are ensured and point (h) requires security, privacy and fraud avoidance; signed credentials, status lists and issuer identity anchoring are one way to meet these, but the Regulation names no technology. Art. 11 fourth subparagraph lets the Commission adopt implementing acts (examination procedure, Art. 73(3)) on procedures to issue and verify the digital credentials of economic operators and other actors with access rights; none was adopted at retrieval. Art. 10(1)(d) requires open standards, interoperable, machine-readable, structured, searchable and transferable data without vendor lock-in, which W3C/IETF/OpenID specifications can support. Art. 11(b) and (f) tie read and write access to access rights set in delegated acts; UNTP's decentralised access control is a candidate mechanism but is not mapped to EU roles. Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 Art. 4 lets economic operators obtain verified status for the DPP registry with qualified electronic signatures or seals, electronic identification of assurance level high, or (qualified) electronic attestations of attributes, valid at most three years (Art. 4(4)); this is the first EU DPP act that admits wallet-style attestations. UNTP itself does not mention EU DPP access rights. Art. 13(2)(a) also lets delegated acts add registry data with regard to verifying DPP authenticity, and Art. 12(5)(c) asks for identifier rules that keep identifiers reliable, verifiable and unique globally; neither names credentials.

L01_unique_identifiers.mechanism: Three identifier kinds coexist. (1) Product identity: in UNTP 0.7.0 the Product subject of a DigitalProductPassport credential carries a resolvable id (URI), idScheme and idGranularity (model, batch or item) plus modelNumber, batchNumber and itemNumber; the 0.7.0 JSON Schema requires id, name, idScheme, idGranularity, productCategory, producedAtFacility and countryOfProduction on the subject. The UNTP VC profile requires DPP, DCC and DTE credentials to carry the goods identifier in credentialSubject. (2) Credential identity: the credential has its own id (required by the UNTP 0.7.0 schema root), distinct from the product id. (3) Party identity: issuers are DIDs (did:web or did:webvh; the schema types issuer.id as a URI and only describes the DID expectation); a Digital Identity Anchor credential issued by an authoritative register binds a DID to a registeredId within a scheme. The UNTP IDR page accepts any scheme that maps an identifier to a resolver query: scheme domain plus a hierarchical path (class, then instance), URNs of the form urn:{ns}:{scheme}:{value} with registry templates, and DIDs whose documents can expose service endpoints (example query ?service=item-dpp). GS1 Digital Link is one such scheme (via the GS1-conformant resolver pattern). The IDR page cites ISO/IEC 18975 (protected; not consulted).

L01_unique_identifiers.observable_black_box: From a sample credential or a resolved one: credentialSubject.id, idScheme, idGranularity, model/batch/item numbers, credential id, issuer.id (DID or URL). A tester can compare the carrier payload with credentialSubject.id (not with the credential id), check that the credential id changes between versions while the product id stays, and check that issuer.id is a DID of an accepted method.
L01_unique_identifiers.law_delta: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 Art. 10(1)(a)-(c) requires a persistent unique product identifier linked through a data carrier and compliant with the standards in Annex III (ISO/IEC 15459 parts, bibliographic only) or equivalent until harmonised standards are referenced; Art. 12(1) applies the same to unique operator and facility identifiers. The VC family adds two identifiers the law does not mention (credential id and issuer DID). A DID is not by itself a unique operator identifier in the Art. 12 sense; UNTP bridges this with a register-issued Digital Identity Anchor. Art. 12(4)-(5) empowers delegated acts on issuing agencies and rules that keep identifiers and carriers reliable, verifiable and unique globally (Art. 12(5)(c)); no such act was located, so a DID-based scheme's acceptability is open.

L02_data_carriers.mechanism: The method is carrier-agnostic. UNTP IDR-04 and IDR-05 (MUST) require reuse of existing carriers and support for both 1D and 2D codes; the carrier holds a resolver URL, not the credential. For encrypted targets, UNTP decentralised access control lets the QR code carry the resolver URL with the symmetric key as a query parameter named decryptionKey, or a short redirect URL on small labels. A separate, non-product carrier pattern exists in wallet protocols: OpenID4VCI credential offers are passed by value (credential_offer) or by reference (credential_offer_uri), typically as a link or QR code. The UNTP reference stack does not define its own carrier format: the printed URL is whatever the identity resolver serves (for GS1 keys a GS1 Digital Link URI on the resolver domain; for other schemes a scheme-domain path or URN mapped to a resolver query), so any carrier that can hold a URL works. A credential itself is never placed on the carrier in this pattern; VCkit advertises QR scanning with an ordinary phone camera as its verification entry point.

The engine's identifier.parse accepts only the GS1 Digital Link form /01/<GTIN>/21/<serial>, so non-GS1 UNTP identifiers (scheme-domain paths, URNs, DIDs, GS1 batch-level /10/ keys) decode but cannot be parsed today.
L02_data_carriers.law_delta: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 Art. 10(1)(a)-(c) governs the carrier and its standards. Putting a decryption key into the carrier is a UNTP pattern with no counterpart in EU law; Art. 10(1)(e) forbids storing customer personal data without consent, which a key does not touch, but the pattern makes the carrier a bearer secret.

L03_data_exchange_protocols.mechanism: (a) Resolution: an HTTP GET on the carrier URL at a GS1-conformant or UNTP Identity Resolver. Without linkType the resolver redirects to the default link (the GS1 standard and the UNTP page do not fix the 3xx code). linkType=linkset (GS1) or the request media type application/linkset+json returns an RFC 9264 linkset; application/ld+json returns JSON-LD; text/html or no Accept returns an HTML page. UNTP also uses linkType=all and named types (dpp, dcc, dfr; examples also show dte, idr, pip, edit) and a language parameter or Accept-Language. Discovery files: /.well-known/gs1resolver (GS1, with resolverRoot and supportedPrimaryKeys) and /.well-known/resolver (UNTP). The UNTP linkset schema extends the GS1 linkset schema; link targets may carry encryptionMethod and accessRole. A secondary resolver is linked with relation idr and a linkset target. (b) Credential retrieval: HTTP GET on the link target; enveloped credentials are served as application/vc+jwt (or vc+sd-jwt, vc+cose), embedded-proof credentials as application/vc or JSON-LD. (c) Key retrieval: dereference kid (a DID URL) or the Data Integrity verificationMethod; did:web maps did:web:example.com to https://example.com/.well-known/did.json and colon-separated path segments to /path/did.json (port percent-encoded); did:webvh maps to https://domain/.well-known/did.jsonl (JSON Lines, served as text/jsonl). (d) Status retrieval: GET statusListCredential URL; any VC media type with proof; servers may support a timestamp query and should align HTTP caching with ttl; errors as RFC 9457 problem details. (e) Issuance and presentation protocols: VCALM (formerly VC API) POST /credentials/issue and workflow exchanges; OpenID4VCI (issuer metadata at /.well-known/openid-credential-issuer, credential, nonce, deferred and notification endpoints, pre-authorized and authorization code flows); OpenID4VP (dcql_query, response_mode direct_post or direct_post.jwt, vp_token, client identifier prefixes such as decentralized_identifier and x509_san_dns, Digital Credentials API annex). UNTP's VC profile treats wallets as optional and discovery through the resolver as primary.

L03_data_exchange_protocols.law_delta: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 Art. 10(1)(d) asks for data transferable through an open interoperable exchange network without vendor lock-in and Art. 11(a) for full technical, semantic and organisational interoperability; neither names a protocol. The VC family adds verification-time dependencies that the law does not mention: DID documents and status lists must be reachable for a credential to be verified.

L04_apis_lifecycle_searchability.mechanism: UNTP defines no create/read/update/delete or search API; credentials are published documents found through the resolver. Write operations exist in the tooling: the UNTP IDR write-link example uses POST with an X-API-Key header; the tests-untp Reference Implementation is a multi-tenant service with Keycloak-issued tokens and a Swagger UI at /api-docs that delegates to VCkit (DID management, signing, verification), a storage service and an identity resolver service. VCkit ships a Bitstring Status List module with its own router. VCALM v1.0 (draft) defines POST /credentials/issue, workflow creation (POST /workflows), exchanges under a workflow, protocol listing, and verify, status and retrieval operations; authorization classes are public, permissioned and bound, using OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens with operation:path scopes or zcaps, and long-lived static credentials such as HTTP Basic are forbidden. The W3C interoperability suites call registered issuer and verifier endpoints of this shape (for example .../credentials/issue and .../credentials/verify) with optional OAuth2 or zcap authorization. OpenID4VCI defines a credential endpoint protected by an access token.

L05_system_interoperability_data_models.mechanism: Envelope: VCDM 2.0, JSON-LD compacted form; @context must start with https://www.w3.org/ns/credentials/v2; media types application/vc and application/vp for unsecured documents; type includes VerifiableCredential. Content: UNTP 0.7.0 schemas (JSON Schema 2020-12, no $id) at /artefacts/schema/v0.7.0/{dpp,dcc,dte,dfr,dia}/...; the DPP schema requires @context, id, issuer, validFrom, name and credentialSubject at the root, fixes the first two @context entries to the W3C v2 context and https://vocabulary.uncefact.org/untp/0.7.0/context/ (minItems 2, unique), requires type to contain DigitalProductPassport and VerifiableCredential when present, allows additional root properties, defines no proof property, and constrains credentialStatus to BitstringStatusListEntry with additionalProperties false. Subject types: Product (DPP), ConformityAttestation (DCC), Facility (DFR), RegisteredIdentity (DIA), MakeEvent/MoveEvent/ModifyEvent or EPCIS TransformationEvent/AggregationEvent/ObjectEvent wrapped as the subject (DTE), Party (Digital Corporate Record, WIP only). Performance claims carry a conformity topic, a numeric or categorical measure, the referenced standard or regulation and criteria, and evidence links (DPP-09 to DPP-13 MUST). The UNTP context is JSON-LD 1.1 with @protected terms (prior record). Extensions: tests-untp maps extension credential types to schema URL patterns (for example a livestock passport). Rendering: renderMethod with RenderTemplate2024 referencing an HTML template by url with digestMultibase (WIP). For Data Integrity proofs, JSON-LD processing must be lossless: undefined terms dropped during expansion must raise an error, and contexts are checked against known values or digests.

L06_storage_archiving_persistence.mechanism: Credentials are files hosted by the issuer or a storage service; because they are signed, any copy remains verifiable if the issuer key and status list stay reachable. The UNTP storage service stores public or encrypted credentials; the playground handles a storage envelope with base64 cipherText, iv and tag using AES-256-GCM. Verification-time dependencies: the DID document (did:web has no history; deactivation is removal of did.json, update is editing the file, so rotating a key out breaks old signatures unless the old key stays listed), the did:webvh log (hash-chained entries with versionId and versionTime; resolvers can ask for a historic version), the status list credential, and the JSON-LD contexts and schemas. The UNTP WIP profile adds MUST rules: status list credentials stay resolvable while relying parties need them, archived copies keep the exact signed bytes, archived verification material never includes issuer private keys, and verification dependencies SHOULD stay retrievable for the credential's intended life. EBSI offers ledger-based timestamping and records (not examined in depth). The UN/CEFACT storage service returns, for every stored document, a digestMultibase (multibase-encoded multihash) of the original bytes, which a credential can carry next to the link so a consumer can check that the fetched document is unchanged; /private storage encrypts with AES-256-GCM and returns the decryption key once.

L06_storage_archiving_persistence.law_delta: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 Art. 10(4) requires a back-up copy through a DPP service provider and Art. 11(c) and (e) require storage by the operator or service providers and availability for the delegated-act period, including after insolvency or cessation. The VC family makes copies independently verifiable but adds availability duties for DID documents and status lists that the law does not name; a did:web domain lapse after insolvency would make all credentials unverifiable.

L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.mechanism: UNTP decentralised access control combines six patterns: anonymous public access (MUST NOT require personal data for public data), unguessable identifiers (random, at least 128-bit), encrypted content with a unique symmetric key per entity (at least 128-bit; AES is the example; SHOULD use a key per authorised role), shared secrets that travel with the product (decryptionKey query parameter), federated authentication with OAuth 2.0 or OIDC, and decentralised authentication with DID-based proofs (SHOULD use DID-Authentication; MAY use DID-SIOP or OpenID4VP). Encrypted link targets MUST be flagged (encryptionMethod from a UNTP code list, example AES-128) and carry accessRole URIs that are matched against registrationScopeList values in Digital Identity Anchor credentials. A requester proves a role by presenting its DIA in a verifiable presentation; the data holder verifies the presentation, DID control and that the anchor issuer is on a trusted list. Write access uses authenticated endpoints. Selective disclosure is possible with SD-JWT (disclosures separated by tildes; @context, type, credentialStatus and credentialSchema recommended non-disclosable) and with ecdsa-sd-2023 base and derived proofs. Status list privacy: large lists for group privacy, random index assignment, verifier caching and proxies to avoid tracking. TEV-12 (SHOULD) asks for access control on sensitive traceability events. The UNTP WIP DCR supports a public record and a fuller restricted record under one identifier.

L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.mechanism: Two securing families. (A) Enveloping, per Securing VCs using JOSE and COSE: JWS compact with typ vc+jwt (SHOULD) and cty vc when present; the payload is the VC JSON itself and the claims vc and vp MUST NOT appear; iss, if present, must equal issuer (or issuer.id); kid MUST be present when the key is a DID URL; keys are found through kid, iss or cnf; in controlled identifier documents the verification method type MUST be JsonWebKey with publicKeyJwk; a JWK thumbprint URI in kid is recommended; iat/exp describe the signature while validFrom/validUntil describe the data; nbf is NOT RECOMMENDED. SD-JWT uses typ vc+sd-jwt; COSE uses COSE_Sign1 (RFC 9052) with typ header application/vc+cose and content type application/vc; presentations embed enveloped credentials as data: URLs typed EnvelopedVerifiableCredential. Examples use ES256, ES384 and EdDSA; no algorithm is mandated in the part read. (B) Embedded Data Integrity: proof object with type DataIntegrityProof, cryptosuite, verificationMethod, proofPurpose (assertionMethod for credentials), created, optional expires, domain, challenge, nonce, previousProof, and proofValue (multibase). Cryptosuites: eddsa-rdfc-2022 and eddsa-jcs-2022 (Ed25519, SHA-256, 64-byte signature, base58btc z prefix, Multikey with 0xed01 header); ecdsa-rdfc-2019 and ecdsa-jcs-2019 (P-256/SHA-256 or P-384/SHA-384, raw P1363 signature 64 or 96 bytes, z prefix); ecdsa-sd-2023 (RDFC with HMAC blank-node relabelling, CBOR proof values with headers 0xd9 0x5d 0x00 for base and 0xd9 0x5d 0x01 for derived, base64url u prefix). Verification checks expected proofPurpose, domain and challenge, and that the verification method's controller matches the issuer under the right relationship; errors include PROOF_VERIFICATION_ERROR, INVALID_DOMAIN_ERROR and INVALID_CHALLENGE_ERROR. Key retrieval (Controlled Identifiers 1.0): split the method URL, dereference the document, require document id equals its URL, dereference the fragment, check id and controller, check the verification relationship. Status (Bitstring Status List 1.0): credentialStatus entries of type BitstringStatusListEntry with statusPurpose (revocation, suspension, refresh, message), statusListIndex as a base-10 string, statusListCredential URL, optional statusSize, statusMessage and statusReference; the list credential (BitstringStatusListCredential, subject BitstringStatusList) carries encodedList = multibase base64url (u) of a GZIP-compressed bitstring of at least 131,072 entries, index 0 is the left-most bit, value 0 means not set; verifiers must verify the list's own proofs and purpose; error types STATUS_RETRIEVAL_ERROR, STATUS_VERIFICATION_ERROR, STATUS_LIST_LENGTH_ERROR. UNTP 0.7.0 profile: VCDM 2.0, JOSE enveloping proof (MUST), DID Core with did:web (MUST implement, SHOULD use own domain) and did:webvh (MUST where auditability is needed), Bitstring Status List (MUST). UNTP WIP adds: issuers MUST produce JOSE or COSE (COSE proposed), verifiers MUST verify both, verifiers SHOULD check signature and status before using a credential found while traversing links, signatures prove integrity and issuer authenticity but not completeness. The 0.7.0 schema types statusListIndex as integer while W3C requires a string; the v0.8.0 schemas switch to a digit string. did:webvh log entries are proven with eddsa-jcs-2022 and SHA-256 multihash SCIDs.

L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.observable_black_box: Everything here is observable from artifacts: JOSE header (alg, typ, cty, kid), payload claims, proof object, DID document and verification relationships, status list credential and the bit value. A verifier can reproduce each finding offline from captured bytes, which suits replayable recordings.
L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.law_delta: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 Art. 11 first subparagraph point (g) requires data authentication, reliability and integrity without naming a mechanism; the VC family is one concrete mechanism. EU law does not require revocation lists; status lists add a lifecycle signal beyond the law. A valid signature proves who signed the bytes, not that the claims are true.

L09_registry_and_customs.mechanism: UNTP has no product registry; it relies on resolvers and on registers of registrars. The UN/CEFACT Global Registrar Information Directory (GRID) lists authoritative registers and their trusted issuer DIDs; non-authoritative registers are listed on UNTP implementation register pages; DIA-03 (SHOULD) asks authorities to register their scheme with UN/CEFACT. A Software register (SWI) is referenced by the WIP issuingSoftware rule. On the EU side, Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 sets up the DPP registry: Art. 4 lets sole traders and legal persons gain verified status with qualified electronic signatures or seals, eID of assurance level high, or (qualified) electronic attestations of attributes, for at most three years; Art. 3(b) provides an API for registration; Art. 3(e) stores identifiers and commodity codes for customs; recitals 15, 16 and 18 describe returned registration identifiers, verification of the backup link and version linking. EBSI positions itself as a trusted-issuer and records infrastructure (Trusted Issuers Registry functions were not confirmed on the pages read).

L09_registry_and_customs.observable_black_box: Only passive: whether the issuer DID appears in a supplied trust list snapshot; whether the DIA issuer domain matches the authority's well-known domain. The EU registry and GRID were not called.
L09_registry_and_customs.law_delta: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 Art. 13 establishes the registry: Art. 13(2)(a) lets delegated acts add registry data chosen with regard to the need to verify DPP authenticity (a possible anchor for issuer keys or credential digests, not specified); Art. 13(5) has the registry return a unique registration identifier, and Art. 15(1)-(2) has customs check that identifier and the commodity code against the registry. Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 Art. 4 is where eIDAS attestations enter DPP practice, for registry users rather than for passport content. Customs links are a registry function in EU law with no UNTP counterpart.

L10_lifecycle_versioning_updates.mechanism: A credential is immutable once signed; change means issuing a new credential (new id) and, when the old one must not be relied on, setting its revocation or suspension bit. Validity windows: validFrom (required by UNTP schemas) and validUntil; the playground rejects a verified credential outside its validity window. Dynamic in-use data uses ModifyEvent traceability credentials (DPP-17). Status purposes: revocation (permanent), suspension (reversible), refresh, message (with statusSize and statusMessage). The UNTP WIP profile asks that status lists stay resolvable while needed. Issuer identity over time: did:web keeps no history; did:webvh keeps a verifiable log with key pre-rotation (nextKeyHashes), portability (portable, alsoKnownAs, newDomain), witnesses and deactivation; the DIA binding between registered identifier and DID is time-bound. Specification versioning: UNTP schemas and contexts are versioned per release (0.6.0 on test.uncefact.org, 0.7.0 on vocabulary.uncefact.org, v0.8.0 in WIP); tests-untp warns that interfaces and schemas can change without a deprecation period; v0.8.0 changes the status entry rules (string index, any purpose, multiple entries).

L10_lifecycle_versioning_updates.law_delta: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 Art. 11(d) requires that a new passport for a product that already has one is linked to the original(s); VCs need an explicit link property for this (UNTP relatedDocument or similar), which the 0.7.0 DPP schema does not require. Recital 18 of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 expects new registry versions to be linked and time-stamped. Revocation semantics are not defined by EU law.

L11_roles_and_governance.mechanism: Roles: the manufacturer issues the DPP; an independent conformity assessment body issues the DCC and states its authority through an authorisation array pointing to endorsement evidence from an accreditation body, government or scheme owner (CC-01, CC-02 MUST), with assessorLevel and assessmentLevel; facility owners or operators issue DFRs; authoritative registers issue DIAs only after verifying DID control (DIA-01) from a DID whose domain matches the authority's domain (DIA-02), with scope URIs for roles (DIA-05); companies issue their own Digital Corporate Record (WIP, proposed). Issuers may delegate key custody to a software provider and then SHOULD fill issuingSoftware (WIP). Trust is layered: signature verifies the key holder; DIA binds DID to registered identity; GRID or trust lists say which registrars to trust; DCC authorisation and accreditation say which assessors to trust; the tests-untp Tier 3 suite infers verified identity and verified claims with N3 rules from a root trusted DID given on the command line. Governance of specifications: W3C VC WG (Recommendations, royalty-free patent policy per prior record), UN/CEFACT for UNTP (licence signals conflict: footer CC BY 4.0, repositories GPL-3.0), OpenID Foundation, IETF, DIF. EBSI is operated by Member States (10 in governance per its portal) under the EUPL; the EU wallet ecosystem is governed by Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 and its implementing acts (not read).

Neither exists yet, so no EU trust framework for DPP credential issuers is defined; UNTP's registrar model is a non-EU alternative.

end_to_end_flows.name: UNTP consumer or regulator verification from a product label (0.7.0 profile)
steps: 1. Scan the 1D or 2D carrier and decode an HTTPS resolver URL (GS1 Digital Link or another scheme path).
2. GET the URL with Accept application/linkset+json or ?linkType=linkset (GS1) / linkType=all (UNTP); without linkType the resolver redirects to the default link.
3. Read the RFC 9264 linkset; select the link typed dpp; note encryptionMethod and accessRole if the target is encrypted; follow idr links to secondary resolvers if needed.
4. GET the DPP credential; expect application/vc+jwt (enveloped) per the UNTP profile.
5. Parse the JOSE header: typ vc+jwt, cty vc, alg, kid; reject a payload that contains a vc or vp claim.

6. Resolve kid: it is a DID URL; for did:web transform to https://<domain>/<path or .well-known>/did.json, check the document id equals the DID, select the JsonWebKey listed under assertionMethod; for did:webvh fetch did.jsonl and verify the log chain first.
7. Verify the JWS signature; check iss equals issuer.id; evaluate validFrom/validUntil against the verification time.

8. Validate the payload: @context begins with the W3C v2 context then the versioned UNTP context; validate against the UNTP JSON Schema of the declared version; optionally expand JSON-LD with pinned contexts.

9. For each credentialStatus entry: GET statusListCredential, verify its proof and issuer, check statusPurpose, decode multibase u + GZIP, require at least 131,072 bits, read the bit at statusListIndex (treat 0 as not revoked).
10. Issuer trust: follow the issuer DID document service to its Digital Identity Anchor, verify it, check its subject id equals the issuer DID and that the registrar DID is on a trusted list (GRID).
11. For each performance claim, follow evidence links to DCCs; verify them the same way; check the DCC names the same product and criteria and that its authorisation endorsement resolves.
12. Optionally render the credential with the HTML template named in renderMethod, after checking its digestMultibase.

end_to_end_flows.name: Issuance and publication with the UN/CEFACT reference stack
steps: 1. The manufacturer system authenticates to the Reference Implementation with a Keycloak-issued token.
2. It submits DPP data; the RI builds a VCDM 2.0 credential with UNTP contexts.
3. VCkit signs it with the tenant's did:web key and allocates a Bitstring Status List entry.
4. The storage service stores the credential publicly or as an AES-256-GCM envelope and returns its URL (and key if encrypted).
5. The identity resolver service registers a dpp link for the product identifier (write calls are authenticated, for example with an API key).
6. The label is printed with the resolver URL, optionally with a decryptionKey query parameter.
7. A background worker settles pending verifications of registered credentials.

end_to_end_flows.name: Authorised-role access to encrypted data (UNTP decentralised access control)
actors: requesting party (for example an accredited recycler)
registrar that issued the requester's DIA
steps: 1. The requester finds an encrypted link target with accessRole URIs in the linkset.
2. The requester authenticates with DID-Authentication (or OpenID4VP) and presents its DIA in a verifiable presentation.
3. The data holder verifies the presentation and DID control and checks that the DIA issuer is on its trusted list and that registrationScopeList matches accessRole.
4. The data holder releases the role key or the decrypted content; the requester decrypts and then verifies the credential signature and status as in the first flow.

end_to_end_flows.name: Credential update and revocation
steps: 1. Product data change; the issuer signs a new credential with a new id for the same product id and links it to the previous one.
2. The issuer sets the revocation (or suspension) bit of the old credential's index and republishes the signed status list credential.
3. The resolver's dpp link is pointed to the new credential.
4. A verifier that cached the old credential sees the bit set on its next status check (bounded by ttl and HTTP caching).

end_to_end_flows.name: EU registry onboarding with eIDAS attestations (context)
actors: qualified trust service provider or attestation provider
steps: 1. The operator obtains a qualified electronic seal, an eID of assurance level high, or a (qualified) electronic attestation of attributes.
2. The operator uses it to obtain verified status in the DPP registry (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 Art. 4).
3. Verified status lasts at most three years; afterwards the operator cannot register or modify until it verifies again (Art. 4(4)).
4. Wallet protocols (OpenID4VCI for issuance, OpenID4VP for presentation) are the expected technical channel in the EUDI ecosystem; how the registry consumes them was not read.

end_to_end_flows.name: EBSI-based battery supply-chain credentials (TRACE4EU pilot, context)
steps: 1. Suppliers and auditors receive EBSI verifiable credentials (LEI, product carbon footprint, responsible mining certificate, due diligence report, consortium membership).
2. The manufacturer collects and verifies them, using the EBSI ledger for legal entity and certificate checks.
3. The manufacturer issues a battery passport credential that references the verified upstream data.
4. Interoperability with Catena-X and UNECE work is stated as a goal; no deliverable or code was located.

failure_modes.fault: statusListIndex emitted as a JSON number because the implementation follows the UNTP 0.7.0 schema; strict W3C verifiers raise a malformed-value error.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Type check of credentialStatus.statusListIndex against the W3C rule; record which UNTP version the credential declares.

failure_modes.fault: Status list shorter than 131,072 entries, or not GZIP-compressed, or missing the u multibase prefix.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Decode encodedList and check prefix, decompression and length (STATUS_LIST_LENGTH_ERROR).

failure_modes.fault: Status list credential is unsigned or signed by a key of a different issuer, so anyone controlling the host can un-revoke credentials.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Verify the list credential's own proof and compare its issuer with the credential issuer.

failure_modes.fault: Legacy VC 1.1 JWT shape: payload wraps the credential in a vc claim or the header uses typ JWT.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Inspect header typ and payload keys; the JOSE/COSE Recommendation forbids vc and vp claims.

failure_modes.fault: iss claim or kid DID differs from the issuer property, letting one key sign for another issuer.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Compare iss, the DID part of kid and issuer.id.

failure_modes.fault: Signing key listed only under authentication, not assertionMethod, in the DID document.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Check the verification relationship during key retrieval (Controlled Identifiers 1.0 algorithm).

failure_modes.fault: did:web document served over plain HTTP, at the wrong path for a path-based DID, or with an id that does not equal the DID.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Apply the did:web transformation and compare the fetched document id with the DID.

failure_modes.fault: Key rotation on did:web removes the old key, so all earlier passports stop verifying (did:web keeps no history).
failure_modes.detectable_by: Re-verify a recorded older credential after a later DID document observation; did:webvh history resolution as a contrast.

failure_modes.fault: Status list host unavailable; the verifier treats a retrieval failure as not revoked.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Mock status service returning 5xx or timeout; the correct outcome is unreachable or STATUS_RETRIEVAL_ERROR, never pass.

failure_modes.fault: Wrong @context order, unversioned UNTP context, or mixing 0.7.0 and 0.8.0 contexts and schemas in one graph.
failure_modes.detectable_by: data.context allowlist per declared version and schema validation per credential.

failure_modes.fault: Properties not defined in any context are silently dropped during RDF canonicalisation, so they are displayed but not signed.
failure_modes.detectable_by: JSON-LD expansion with pinned contexts and a dropped-term check before trusting an rdfc proof.

failure_modes.fault: Resolver answers 200 with an HTML page for every request, ignores linkType=linkset, or omits the dpp link.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Content negotiation and linkType probes against the GS1 resolver rules; linkset schema validation.

failure_modes.fault: credentialSubject.id differs from the carrier identifier (for example batch-level id on an item-level label) or the same credential id is reused for a new version.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Carrier-to-subject comparison and comparison of credential ids across recorded versions.

failure_modes.fault: Encrypted link target not flagged, or restricted credential served in clear at an unguessable but unauthenticated URL.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Inspect linkset target attributes and fetch the target without credentials.

failure_modes.fault: decryptionKey embedded in the printed URL is logged by the resolver or leaked to third parties through redirects and Referer headers.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Check whether the resolver redirect keeps the key in the Location URL and whether a Referrer-Policy header is set.

failure_modes.fault: Digital Identity Anchor issued by a non-registrar, from a DID whose domain does not match the authority, or naming a different subject DID.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Check DIA issuer against the trust list snapshot, DIA-02 domain match, and subject id equality.

failure_modes.fault: DCC claims accreditation in its authorisation array but the endorsement link does not resolve or names another body.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Follow endorsementEvidence and compare the endorsed body with the DCC issuer.

failure_modes.fault: Updated passport issued without revoking the superseded one, leaving two conflicting valid credentials for one product.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Recorded sequence: both credentials verify and neither status bit is set.

failure_modes.fault: Label encodes a vendor short link or app deep link that redirects off the resolver, or encodes a signed JWT directly, so generic scanners and verifiers cannot follow the UNTP resolution path.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Decode the sample QR and classify the payload (resolver URL, short link, non-HTTP scheme, raw JWT); follow redirects on loopback fixtures only.

failure_modes.fault: decryptionKey printed in a public QR for data meant to be restricted to a role, so anyone who scans the label can read it.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Flag a decryptionKey parameter in the decoded URL and compare with the access tier declared for the target.

failure_modes.fault: A VCALM-style verifier endpoint returns verified true when the proof is valid but skips the status check, or returns HTTP 200 with an error body instead of a problem detail.
failure_modes.detectable_by: POST a validly signed but revoked fixture credential and a tampered one to a loopback instance; assert the verdict and the HTTP status.

failure_modes.fault: Write endpoints (issue, link registration) accept static API keys or unauthenticated calls, against the VCALM rule that forbids long-lived static credentials.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Call the write endpoint of a loopback SUT without credentials and with an expired token; expect 401 or 403.

failure_modes.fault: Issuer DID or Digital Identity Anchor lists a registered identifier that differs from the operator identifier uploaded to the EU DPP registry, so passport and registry describe different operators.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Compare the DIA registeredId with the operator identifier in a supplied registry extract (sample artifact); no live registry call.

open_questions: Which algorithms does the UNTP profile accept for vc+jwt (ES256, EdDSA, ES384)? The 0.7.0 and WIP pages read name none; a conformance pack needs a maintainer-chosen allowlist.

Should the engine extend integrity.jws (configurable typ, cty, kid-based key lookup) or add a separate integrity.vc_jose capability? The current check is purpose-built for typ dpp+jws with x5c and an X.509 trust bundle; a contract decision is needed.

How should a test pack treat statusListIndex for UNTP 0.7.0 credentials: follow the UNTP schema (integer) or the W3C Recommendation (string)? Proposal: report both, keyed by the declared UNTP version.
Under which licence may UNTP schemas, contexts and sample credentials be used as fixtures (CC BY 4.0 footer versus GPL-3.0 repositories)? Unresolved since 2026-10-13.
Will the ESPR Art. 11 implementing act on digital credentials prescribe W3C VCs, eIDAS attestations, or another mechanism? Commission slides only give Q2 2027.

Does the EU DPP registry accept wallet-presented attestations (OpenID4VP) technically, and in which format (SD-JWT VC, mdoc)? Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 Art. 4 names the legal means only; the technical guidance was not read.
What is the format of the UNTP /.well-known/resolver description file, and does it equal the GS1 /.well-known/gs1resolver schema?
Which EBSI services (Trusted Issuers Registry, DID registry, timestamping) did TRACE4EU use for the battery passport, and are deliverables public?

SD-JWT VC is still an Internet-Draft (-19, waiting for AD go-ahead on 2026-10-19) with typ dc+sd-jwt: should a DPP test pack accept dc+sd-jwt next to vc+sd-jwt from VC-JOSE-COSE, and which one does the EUDI Wallet ecosystem expect?
Will the ESPR delegated acts under Art. 12(4)-(5) (issuing agencies) or Art. 13(2) (extra registry data for authenticity) accept DIDs or credential digests? None was located.

UNTP 0.7.0 VC requirements VC-01 to VC-10 carry no MUST/SHOULD levels; the normative keywords sit in unnumbered prose.
